records.Entity / project type: desktop Bitcoin privacy wallet / Wasabi fork
records.Concise description: An actively maintained Bitcoin-only privacy wallet forked from Wasabi after the 2024 shutdown of zkSNACKs' default CoinJoin coordinator.
records.Deeper researched summary: Ginger Wallet is a non-custodial, open-source desktop wallet derived from Wasabi's codebase. It provides a default WabiSabi CoinJoin coordinator operated within Ginger's current legal/operational model, while retaining Bitcoin-only desktop use, Tor-by-default networking and privacy-focused transaction workflows. The project exists as a distinct active successor/fork rather than merely a Wasabi configuration.
records.Launch / history: Forked from the Wasabi codebase in 2024 after zkSNACKs announced the shutdown of its default coordinator; maintained as a distinct project through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Ginger is important because it shows the post-2024 continuation of the WabiSabi privacy-wallet model under a distinct project and coordinator operator.
records.Verification basis: Current first-party site/docs and active repository verify the distinct project, desktop platforms, non-custodial model and current coordinator operation.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not collapse Ginger into Wasabi: it is a fork with a separate maintainer/operator identity.
CoinJoin/privacy claims should describe mechanisms, not promise anonymity.

records.Entity / project type: inactive mobile Bitcoin privacy wallet / services ecosystem
records.Concise description: A historically important Android Bitcoin privacy wallet whose operated services shut down after U.S. authorities seized infrastructure and arrested its founders in April 2024.
records.Deeper researched summary: Samourai combined a self-custody Android wallet with privacy and transaction tools including Whirlpool CoinJoin, coin control, Tor-oriented networking and its Dojo backend. In April 2024 U.S. authorities arrested Keonne Rodriguez and William Lonergan Hill and seized Samourai infrastructure; both later pleaded guilty in 2025 and were sentenced in November 2025. Source code remains available, but code availability does not make the operated wallet/service ecosystem active.
records.Launch / history: Samourai emerged in the mid-2010s, developed a prominent privacy wallet and Dojo/Whirlpool stack, then had key infrastructure seized in April 2024. The named founders pleaded guilty in 2025 and were sentenced in November 2025.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It was a major Bitcoin privacy-wallet project and influenced coin-control, collaborative transaction and self-hosted backend practices; its shutdown is also important legal and operational history.

Corroborating sources.label: U.S. DOJ — Samourai founders arrested and charged

records.Verification basis: Official source-code history plus U.S. Justice Department seizure, plea and sentencing records establish the lifecycle change and legal status.
Research notes / uncertainties: Describe criminal allegations/convictions precisely by date and procedural posture; do not generalize legal conclusions to privacy wallets as a class.
The wallet software's historical self-custody model is distinct from allegations concerning the operated mixing/service business.
Code availability is not evidence of an active Samourai service.

records.Concise description: A long-running self-custody mobile wallet whose Android client remains actively maintained and supports advanced Bitcoin transaction and hardware-wallet workflows.
records.Deeper researched summary: Mycelium is among the oldest surviving mobile wallet brands in Bitcoin. Its current Android client keeps keys under user control and supports native SegWit, fee controls, Tor, watch-only use and hardware-wallet integrations. The project's iOS repository was archived in May 2026 while the Android repository continued receiving 2026 updates, so platform maintenance should not be described as uniform.
records.Launch / history: Mycelium's company/project roots date to 2008 and its Bitcoin wallet became prominent in the early 2010s. The Android repository remained active in May 2026; the iOS repository was archived in May 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is historically and practically significant as a durable mobile self-custody wallet with deep Bitcoin-specific tooling and hardware-wallet interoperability.
Important technical or cultural characte: Android is the clearly active current client
Native SegWit and legacy address support
records.Verification basis: Current official site and 2026 GitHub activity verify ongoing Android operation; archived iOS repository provides the platform-specific caution.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not imply that iOS and Android are equally maintained in 2026; the iOS source repository was archived.
The current wallet also exposes non-Bitcoin asset functionality; MSC's profile is limited to its Bitcoin role.

records.Concise description: Proton's open-source self-custody Bitcoin wallet, integrating encrypted wallet metadata and a Bitcoin-via-Email addressing experience with standard seed-based recovery.
records.Deeper researched summary: Proton Wallet is operated by Proton Financial AG and uses end-to-end encryption so Proton states it cannot access users' private keys, seed phrases, balances or encrypted wallet metadata. It supports web, iOS and Android and can send Bitcoin to other Proton Wallet users through signed email-address mappings while retaining ordinary Bitcoin addresses and standard recovery seeds.
Creators / founders: Andy Yen — Proton founder / launch author
records.Launch / history: Introduced in early access in July 2024 and opened broadly in February 2025; remained an active Bitcoin-only self-custody product in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Proton brought a large privacy-software brand into Bitcoin self-custody and introduced an email-identity UX layer without replacing the underlying Bitcoin key/recovery model.
Important technical or cultural characte: Bitcoin via Email with signed address mappings
Automatic address rotation for Bitcoin-via-Email receipts
Third-party on-ramp integrations separated from wallet custody
records.Verification basis: Current Proton Wallet and security documentation plus launch history verify self-custody, platform availability, open-source status and recovery model.
Research notes / uncertainties: Bitcoin via Email is an application-layer addressing/convenience feature, not a Bitcoin protocol change.
On-ramp partners are separate services and should not be conflated with Proton's wallet custody model.
